Title: Patient Registration and Login
Preconditions: None
Steps: 1. Navigate to login page | 2. Click 'Sign up' toggle | 3. Fill in full name 'John Doe' | 4. Fill in email 'john.doe@test.com' | 5. Fill in password 'Test@1234' | 6. Select role 'patient' | 7. Submit form | 8. Verify redirect to dashboard
Test Data: Full Name: John Doe | Email: john.doe@test.com | Password: Test@1234 | Role: patient
Expected Result: User is successfully registered and redirected to dashboard with patient role badge visible

Title: Doctor Appointment Booking Flow
Preconditions: Patient is logged in and patient profile exists
Steps: 1. Navigate to dashboard | 2. Click 'Book Appointment' action card | 3. Select department 'Cardiology' | 4. Choose a doctor from dropdown | 5. Select future date (e.g. tomorrow) | 6. Choose an available time slot | 7. Enter reason 'Chest pain consultation' | 8. Submit booking | 9. Verify success message and redirect to appointments list
Test Data: Department: Cardiology | Date: Tomorrow | Reason: Chest pain consultation
Expected Result: Appointment is created with status 'SCHEDULED' and appears in appointments list

Title: Queue Management - Add Patient to Queue
Preconditions: Staff/Admin is logged in
Steps: 1. Navigate to queue management page | 2. Select a doctor from dropdown | 3. Click add to queue (or system adds when appointment starts) | 4. Verify token number is generated | 5. Verify patient appears in queue with correct priority
Test Data: Doctor ID: valid | Patient ID: valid | Priority: normal
Expected Result: Patient is added to queue with token number in format T001 and status 'waiting'

Title: Create Prescription and View
Preconditions: Doctor is logged in and visit record exists
Steps: 1. Navigate to patient visit record | 2. Create new prescription | 3. Add medication: Aspirin 100mg twice daily for 7 days | 4. Add instructions 'Take after meals' | 5. Save prescription | 6. Patient logs in | 7. Navigate to prescriptions page | 8. Verify prescription is visible
Test Data: Medication: Aspirin 100mg | Frequency: Twice daily | Duration: 7 days | Instructions: Take after meals
Expected Result: Prescription is created and visible to both doctor and patient with all medication details

Title: Update Patient Profile Information
Preconditions: Patient is logged in
Steps: 1. Navigate to profile page | 2. Click 'Edit Profile' | 3. Update address to '123 Main St' | 4. Update blood group to 'O+' | 5. Add emergency contact 'Jane Doe' with phone '555-1234' | 6. Add insurance provider 'Blue Cross' | 7. Save changes | 8. Verify data persists after page refresh
Test Data: Address: 123 Main St | Blood Group: O+ | Emergency Contact: Jane Doe (555-1234) | Insurance: Blue Cross
Expected Result: Profile is updated successfully and all changes are visible on the profile page

Title: Complete Patient Journey - Registration to Prescription
Preconditions: None - clean state
Steps: 1. Patient registers account | 2. Complete patient profile with demographics | 3. Browse available doctors by specialty | 4. Book appointment for specific date/time | 5. Doctor reviews appointment | 6. Patient added to queue on appointment day | 7. Doctor calls patient from queue | 8. Doctor records visit history with diagnosis | 9. Doctor creates prescription | 10. Patient views prescription | 11. Patient can download/print prescription
Test Data: Patient: Test User | Doctor: Cardiology specialist | Appointment: Next week | Diagnosis: Hypertension | Prescription: Lisinopril 10mg daily
Expected Result: Complete patient journey executes without errors from registration through prescription receipt

Title: Doctor Schedule Management to Appointment Fulfillment
Preconditions: Doctor account exists
Steps: 1. Doctor logs in | 2. Navigate to schedule management | 3. Create schedule for tomorrow 9AM-5PM with 30min slots | 4. Block lunch slot 12-1PM | 5. Patient books appointment at 10AM | 6. Doctor views appointments list for tomorrow | 7. On appointment day queue shows patient | 8. Doctor marks queue entry in progress | 9. Doctor completes consultation | 10. Doctor marks queue entry complete
Test Data: Schedule: Tomorrow 9AM-5PM | Blocked: 12-1PM | Appointment: 10AM | Patient: existing
Expected Result: Doctor successfully manages schedule and processes patient through full workflow

Title: Multi-Role Appointment Lifecycle
Preconditions: Patient doctor and staff accounts exist
Steps: 1. Patient books appointment | 2. Staff views all appointments | 3. Staff adds patient to queue manually | 4. Doctor views queue | 5. Doctor calls next patient | 6. Doctor records visit notes | 7. Patient requests reschedule | 8. Staff/Admin reschedules appointment | 9. All parties see updated appointment status
Test Data: Original Date: Tomorrow | New Date: Next week | Roles: Patient Doctor Staff
Expected Result: All roles can interact with appointment lifecycle and status updates are reflected across all user types

Title: Book Appointment with Already Taken Time Slot
Preconditions: Another patient has booked same doctor/date/time
Steps: 1. Patient A books doctor at 2PM tomorrow | 2. Patient B attempts to book same doctor at 2PM tomorrow | 3. Select same doctor and date | 4. Verify 2PM slot is not in available slots list | 5. Attempt direct API call with taken slot | 6. Verify error response
Test Data: Doctor ID: same | Date: tomorrow | Time: 2PM | Patient A: booked | Patient B: attempting
Expected Result: System prevents double-booking and 2PM slot does not appear in Patient B's available slots list

Title: Queue Priority Ordering Emergency vs Normal
Preconditions: Multiple patients in queue with different priorities
Steps: 1. Add normal priority patient to queue (Token T001) | 2. Add senior citizen patient to queue (Token T002) | 3. Add emergency patient to queue (Token T003) | 4. View queue list | 5. Verify ordering is Emergency first then Senior then Normal
Test Data: Normal Patient: P001 | Senior Patient: P002 (age > 60) | Emergency Patient: P003
Expected Result: Queue displays in priority order: Emergency (T003) at position 1 Senior (T002) at position 2 Normal (T001) at position 3

Title: Doctor Leave Blocking - No Appointments Allowed
Preconditions: Doctor has active schedule for date
Steps: 1. Doctor creates schedule for next Monday | 2. Doctor marks next Monday as leave with reason 'Personal' | 3. Patient attempts to book appointment for next Monday with this doctor | 4. Verify no slots available | 5. Verify schedule shows is_available=false
Test Data: Date: Next Monday | Leave Reason: Personal | Doctor: on leave
Expected Result: No time slots are available for booking and patient sees appropriate message

Title: Access Patient Records - Role Based Restrictions
Preconditions: Multiple users with different roles logged in
Steps: 1. Patient logs in and navigates to /patients/search | 2. Verify 403 forbidden error | 3. Staff logs in and searches patients | 4. Verify staff can view patient list | 5. Patient attempts API call to view other patient's profile | 6. Verify 403 error | 7. Doctor views own patient records | 8. Verify doctor can access patient details
Test Data: Patient Role: patient | Staff Role: staff | Doctor Role: doctor | Other Patient ID: different user
Expected Result: Role-based access control is enforced: Patients cannot search others Staff and doctors can access patient records Admin has full access

Title: Search and Filter Appointments by Status
Preconditions: Multiple appointments exist with different statuses
Steps: 1. Navigate to appointments page | 2. Click 'Scheduled' filter | 3. Verify only scheduled appointments display | 4. Click 'Completed' filter | 5. Verify only completed appointments display | 6. Click 'Cancelled' filter | 7. Verify only cancelled appointments display | 8. Click 'All' filter | 9. Verify all appointments display
Test Data: Scheduled: 3 appointments | Completed: 2 appointments | Cancelled: 1 appointment | Total: 6 appointments
Expected Result: Filter correctly displays appointments matching selected status and count matches expectations

Title: Create Visit History with Clinical Notes
Preconditions: Doctor is logged in and appointment is completed
Steps: 1. Doctor navigates to visit history page | 2. Click create new visit record | 3. Select patient from appointment | 4. Enter diagnosis 'Type 2 Diabetes' | 5. Add symptoms: frequent urination excessive thirst | 6. Add vital signs: BP 130/85 Weight 85kg | 7. Add clinical notes 'Patient advised lifestyle modifications' | 8. Mark as report ready | 9. Save visit record | 10. Verify visit appears in patient's history
Test Data: Diagnosis: Type 2 Diabetes | Symptoms: frequent urination excessive thirst | BP: 130/85 | Weight: 85kg | Report Ready: true
Expected Result: Visit history is created with all clinical details and marked as report ready for patient viewing

Title: Reschedule Appointment to Different Date
Preconditions: Patient has scheduled appointment
Steps: 1. Patient navigates to appointments | 2. Click on scheduled appointment | 3. Click 'Reschedule' button | 4. Select new date (one week later) | 5. Choose new available time slot | 6. Confirm reschedule | 7. Verify appointment status changed to 'RESCHEDULED' | 8. Verify new date and time are updated | 9. Verify old slot becomes available for others
Test Data: Original: Tomorrow 2PM | New: Next week 3PM | Doctor: same
Expected Result: Appointment is rescheduled successfully status shows RESCHEDULED and updated_at timestamp is set

Title: Doctor Views Today's Appointments Dashboard
Preconditions: Doctor has appointments scheduled for today
Steps: 1. Doctor logs in | 2. View dashboard | 3. Verify 'Today's Appointments' stat shows correct count | 4. Navigate to appointments page | 5. Verify date filter shows today by default | 6. Verify all listed appointments are for today's date
Test Data: Today's Date: 2026-05-13 | Doctor Appointments Today: 4 | Other Dates: 0
Expected Result: Dashboard correctly displays today's appointment count and appointments page defaults to today's filter

Title: Register with Already Existing Email
Preconditions: User account with email exists
Steps: 1. Navigate to registration page | 2. Enter email 'existing@test.com' that is already registered | 3. Fill other required fields | 4. Submit registration form | 5. Verify error message displays | 6. Verify registration is rejected
Test Data: Email: existing@test.com (already in database) | Full Name: Test User | Password: Test@1234
Expected Result: Error message 'Email already registered' is displayed and no duplicate account is created

Title: Login with Incorrect Credentials
Preconditions: User account exists
Steps: 1. Navigate to login page | 2. Enter correct email 'user@test.com' | 3. Enter incorrect password 'WrongPass123' | 4. Submit login form | 5. Verify error message | 6. Verify no token is generated | 7. Verify user remains on login page
Test Data: Email: user@test.com (correct) | Password: WrongPass123 (incorrect)
Expected Result: Error message 'Incorrect email or password' is displayed and authentication fails

Title: Book Appointment Without Selecting Time Slot
Preconditions: Patient is on booking form
Steps: 1. Navigate to book appointment page | 2. Select department | 3. Select doctor | 4. Select date | 5. Do NOT select any time slot | 6. Enter reason | 7. Attempt to submit form | 8. Verify submit button is disabled | 9. Verify form validation prevents submission
Test Data: Department: Cardiology | Doctor: selected | Date: tomorrow | Time: not selected
Expected Result: Submit button remains disabled until time slot is selected and form cannot be submitted

Title: Access Protected Route Without Authentication
Preconditions: User is not logged in - no token
Steps: 1. Clear browser local storage (remove access_token) | 2. Attempt to navigate to /dashboard | 3. Verify redirect to /login | 4. Attempt to navigate to /appointments | 5. Verify redirect to /login | 6. Attempt API call to /api/patients/me without Authorization header | 7. Verify 401 Unauthorized response
Test Data: No authentication token present
Expected Result: All protected routes redirect to login page and API calls without token return 401 error

Title: Cancel Already Completed Appointment
Preconditions: Appointment exists with status completed
Steps: 1. Patient views appointments list | 2. Find appointment with status 'COMPLETED' | 3. Verify cancel and reschedule buttons are NOT displayed | 4. Attempt direct API DELETE call to /appointments/{completed_id} | 5. Verify appropriate error or no status change | 6. Verify appointment remains completed
Test Data: Appointment ID: existing | Status: completed | Patient: authorized owner
Expected Result: Completed appointments cannot be cancelled - UI hides cancel button and status remains unchanged
